findings.message: The fix covers only one way the task list can drift from storage: order. The comment's own class is 'every sync would see a change it can't make', and two variants are still open. (1) A task removed from change.md: `writeTasks` (server/tasks.ts:13) only upserts and never deletes, so the stored list keeps the removed ref while `desired` drops it. (2) A ref listed twice in change.md: `desired` keeps both entries, but storage holds one row per (proposal_id, ref). In both cases the fingerprint never matches again. Every later sync (syncSpecclaw and push.ts `unchanged`) rewrites the row and appends a `delivery.proposal.sync` audit row. `tasksTotal` also changes back and forth between `tasks.length` from desired and the stored count from `countTasks`. Fix: normalise both sides to the same task set in `desired`/`fingerprint`. Merge with the stored refs, or drop or flag missing ones, and dedupe by ref. Alternatively, make `writeTasks` reconcile deletions.
findings.scenario: Sync change.md with T1, T2, T3. Then delete the T3 line and sync twice → the 2nd and later syncs return updated: 1 (never unchanged: 1), and each one writes a new audit row.

findings.message: The fix ships one hand-picked case (T2, T10, T1) through `syncSpecclaw` only. It needs a table-driven test over the variants: the named T26-before-T25, a ref-length case (T10 before T9), a reverse-ordered list, and an already-sorted control. The test also never drives the second caller of `desired`, the repo push path (`server/push.ts:87` → `unchanged`), which has its own fingerprint comparison. A regression there stays green.
findings.scenario: Revert the `.sort(byRef)` and also change push.ts to build tasks some other way → the push path flags out-of-order change.md files as updated on every push, and no test fails.

findings.message: The task order is now written twice: `byRef` in JS and `order by length(t.ref), t.ref` in the `storedSpecRows` SQL (line 38). The SQL side uses the database collation. They agree only because refs are limited to /^T\d+$/. If either copy changes, every sync becomes a change again. Sort both sides with the same function inside `fingerprint`, so storage order no longer matters.
